6. Why Soft Labels Carry More Information

blocks.alt: A soft target gives a richer training signal

blocks.text: This connects back to soft targets versus hard labels, already covered in this topic. A genuinely hard label only genuinely says which single class is correct.

The teacher's own genuinely full distribution also genuinely reveals which incorrect classes are still relatively plausible, a genuinely subtle but valuable extra signal explored throughout the rest of this topic.

10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a simplified distillation loss combining teacher soft targets and true hard labels, already covered in this topic.

code.content:
import math

def softmax(scores):
    # already covered generally as the softmax function in Attention Mechanism
    exp_scores = [math.exp(s) for s in scores]
    total = sum(exp_scores)
    return [e / total for e in exp_scores]

teacher_logits = [3.0, 1.0, 0.5]  # already covered as the teacher model's own output in this topic
student_logits = [2.0, 1.5, 0.8]  # already covered as the student model's own output in this topic

teacher_soft_targets = softmax(teacher_logits)  # already covered as soft targets in this topic
student_soft_predictions = softmax(student_logits)
true_label_index = 0  # already covered as a hard label in this topic

def soft_loss(teacher_probs, student_probs):
    # already covered as the soft loss component in this topic
    return -sum(t * math.log(s) for t, s in zip(teacher_probs, student_probs))

def hard_loss(student_probs, true_index):
    # already covered as the hard loss component in this topic
    return -math.log(student_probs[true_index])

combined_loss = 0.7 * soft_loss(teacher_soft_targets, student_soft_predictions) + 0.3 * hard_loss(student_soft_predictions, true_label_index)

print(f"Teacher soft targets (already covered in this topic): {[round(p, 3) for p in teacher_soft_targets]}")
print(f"Student predictions: {[round(p, 3) for p in student_soft_predictions]}")
print(f"\nCombined distillation loss (already covered in this topic): {combined_loss:.4f}")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Distillation trains a small student model to mimic a larger, already-trained teacher model.
Unlike pruning, it trains a brand-new, smaller model rather than shrinking an existing one.
A fixed teacher model guides a much smaller student model during training.
The student trains on the teacher's full soft probability distribution, not just hard labels.
Soft labels reveal which incorrect classes are still relatively plausible, a richer signal.
The training loss combines a soft loss against the teacher with a hard loss against true labels.
The student's architecture can be dramatically smaller than the teacher's, with far fewer parameters.
Distillation suits allowing a completely different architecture; pruning suits keeping the same one.
